title: Kimpton Social Password Winter 2026-2027: “This Calls For Something”
summary: Kimpton's social password for winter is "this calls for something," valid November 27, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Here's how it works and what I won at check-in.
content: Kimpton has a pretty cool “social password” concept, whereby you can receive extra perks for sharing a phrase at check-in. Kimpton generally has this promotion a couple of times per year — we last saw this in summer, and there’s now a new password for winter. I’d like to talk about what the new password is, share my experience using it, and also pose a question to Kimpton regulars about the least cringeworthy way to go about saying it. What is the current Kimpton password? Kimpton is one of the cooler IHG hotel groups, and there are a variety of things that set Kimpton apart from other IHG brands. One of those things is the social password. The idea is that seasonally, Kimpton provides a phrase through social media that you’re supposed to say when you check-in, and if you do that, you’ll receive something extra. The new Kimpton password is “this calls for something,” and it’s valid for stays between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027. So just say that when you check-in at a Kimpton property during the promotion period, and you’ll receive a surprise. My experience using the Kimpton password For those curious about what happens when you say the Kimpton password, I stayed at the Kimpton EPIC Miami some time back, which was my first Kimpton stay in quite a while (and I haven’t stayed at one since either). It was a good value as well , as I was able to use a free night award earned with the New IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card ( learn more ). I was curious what the benefit would be for using the password. So I shared the password with the front desk agent. At the conclusion of the check-in experience, he brought out a game show-style wheel. I might have spun too hard, as it must have gone around for about 30 seconds. Go figure I landed on the tile that just had me spin again. Then I spun again, and the prize was free parking. I had a car and was staying for two nights, and parking costs $44 per night. So using the Kimpton password saved me nearly $100 — score!! Kimpton social password wheel Based on looking at the wheel, it seems that some of the other prizes include a free welcome drink, free breakfast, free snacks, and a free movie. There were also a few empty squares, where I guess you don’t win anything. And I’m not sure what the alarm clock, car tipping over, or postcard of Miami get you. Regardless, I’d say those are some awesome prizes, and I got a great reward. It’s cute how the Kimpton EPIC Miami makes a game of this. I know there’s a lot of inconsistency when it comes to this benefit across Kimpton properties. Some hotels provide meaningful perks (an upgrade, free, parking, etc.), like I got here, while other hotels provide a 19 cent branded koozie. It’s great that this has stuck around, given that it has presumably become increasingly popular. Years ago not everyone was on social media, so it was a good way to encourage people to follow Kimpton on X, Facebook, Instagram, etc. With the way the internet has evolved, times have changed a bit. How do you non-awkwardly say the Kimpton password? I’m sure I’m not the only one who finds the concept of saying a password at check-in to be kind of weird. So I think it’s fun to compare notes about how people share the password at the front desk. I find it awkward to just blurt out the password out of nowhere. So when I used this for my stay, I said “I guess I’m supposed to say [social password] as the social password?” That did the trick, but I’d be curious to hear how other Kimpton regulars go about this! Bottom line Between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027, Kimpton’s social password is “this calls for something.” Just state that phrase when you check-in at a Kimpton, and you should get some sort of a surprise. The gift will vary by property, so there’s no reason not to take advantage of this if staying at a Kimpton. The last time I used the password I got to spin a wheel at check-in, and then I ended up getting free parking, which was a value of $44 per night. If you’ve used the Kimpton password, what was your experience like?

title: Book A Southwest Airlines Ticket, Get Promotional Companion Pass
summary: Southwest Airlines has launched another Companion Pass promotion. Register, then book one roundtrip ticket between November 27 and 29, 2026, and you can earn a Companion Pass valid into early March 2027.
content: Southwest Airlines has just introduced an incredibly generous promotion, which we see several times per year. With this, you can earn a promotional Companion Pass after booking a single roundtrip ticket, and that could be a great deal. Book a ticket, get Companion Pass for several weeks With a new promotion from Southwest, you can earn a promotional Companion Pass by booking a single roundtrip ticket (or two one-ways). Here are the details of how this works: You must register for the promotion , and then purchase one roundtrip or two one-way tickets between November 27 and November 29, 2026 (yes, the ticket has to be booked after registering, so it’s a short booking window; however, you can always cancel an existing ticket and rebook with vouchers) In order for a ticket to qualify, it can be booked with cash, points, or Cash + Points You must travel by January 5, 2027 Then you can earn a promotional Companion Pass that’s valid for travel between January 8 and March 3, 2027; you’ll be able to change your companion up to three times during the promotion period This is an extremely generous offer. We usually see an offer like this a few times per year, so it’s nice to see it return. It seems that even with all the other changes at Southwest, this promotion is at least one thing that’s remaining consistent. There’s a great Southwest Companion Pass promo What is Southwest Airlines Companion Pass? For those of you not familiar with Companion Pass , it’s one of the best deals in travel. Those with Companion Pass can have a companion fly with them for just the cost of taxes, regardless of whether paying cash or redeeming points. Essentially think of it as a two-for-one travel pass, which is otherwise pretty unheard of. Under the current rules, Southwest Companion Pass ordinarily requires 100 flights or 135,000 qualifying points in a calendar year, so this promotion offers quite the shortcut (though also with a limited travel window). We are seeing changes to Companion Pass in 2027 , as Companion Pass will become a perk of top tier Platinum elite status, rather than something that’s separately qualified for. Earn a limited time Companion Pass with this promotion Bottom line Southwest Airlines has introduced a generous promotion that can earn you Companion Pass. Those who register and then book a roundtrip ticket between November 27 and November 29, 2026, for travel by January 5, 2027, can earn a promotional Companion Pass valid for several weeks early next year. Obviously this promotion isn’t for everyone, but if you have any travel to potentially plan over the promotion period, then this offer is seriously worth considering. It’s awesome how often Southwest offers this promotion. Do you plan on taking advantage of this Southwest Companion Pass promo?

title: Mobile Passport Control: Free App That Speeds Up US Immigration
summary: Mobile Passport Control is a free app that gives eligible travelers access to a separate, usually shorter US immigration line. Here's how it works and how to use it.
content: Frequent travelers to the United States are probably familiar with Global Entry , which allows enrolled members to get expedited immigration at US airports. However, applying for Global Entry is a bit of a process, and there’s a cost to participate. If you don’t want Global Entry (or aren’t eligible), your next best option is Mobile Passport Control. This is sort of a hidden program that doesn’t get talked about enough, given that it can significantly cut down your wait times at US immigration. In this post, I’d like to talk about how this works, as I’ve used it a couple of times now (when traveling internationally with our younger son, who doesn’t yet have Global Entry). How Mobile Passport Control works Mobile Passport Control (MPC) is a free app that allows travelers to submit their travel document, photo, and customs declaration information, before they arrive at the immigration checkpoint at a US airport. Travelers just have to download the app, which is available for Apple and Android. The idea is that the app streamlines the traveler’s entry process to the United States by reducing passport control inspection times and overall wait times. Those who use MPC can access a separate immigration screening checkpoint. Really that’s the biggest advantage — because not many people use this program (as of now), the wait times are generally much shorter than the standard wait times. There are some important things to be aware of, as you’d expect: MPC is available to US passport holders and permanent residents, as well as Canadian passport holders MPC is available in 63 locations, including at 37 US international airports, 15 Preclearance locations , four land borders, four seaports, and three departure locations There’s no pre-approval required to use MPC; you just have to complete a customs declaration through the app every time you enter the United States, and then you’ll be given a QR code that you show the immigration officer Those who use MPC don’t have to complete a paper immigration form, or use a kiosk where they make their declaration; however, they still have to talk to an immigration officer (like other passengers), but in theory the process should be faster, and you shouldn’t be asked as many questions In the interest of being thorough, here are the current airports participating in Mobile Passport Control: Abu Dhabi Zayed International Airport (AUH) Anchorage International Airport (ANC) Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport (ATL) Aruba Queen Beatrix International Airport (AUA) Bermuda L.F. I’d recommend downloading the app prior to boarding your flight to the United States, and completing the basic requirements. Then you have to submit your customs declaration after you land in the United States (within four hours of when you intend to clear immigration). Once you download the app, there are several pages explaining how the app works, plus you have to agree to a disclaimer statement. Note that you can use one app to submit your application for multiple people in the same family. Furthermore, you can save the passport details in the app for multiple trips, eliminating the need to submit all of this information each time (though you do need to make a customs declaration each time). To start the process, you’ll have to state which CBP port you’ll be arriving at, and they all show on a dropdown menu. Mobile Passport Control app At that point you’ll have to select the travelers who will be entering the country. If you’ve already saved people to your profile, they’ll show on that page. Otherwise you can start from scratch, which just requires scanning the document, and then all the information will be auto-populated. Mobile Passport Control app Mobile Passport Control app Mobile Passport Control app You’ll then need to capture traveler photos. This doesn’t need to be a passport-quality photo — you just have to follow some very basic guidelines, like removing hats and sunglasses, and making sure only one person’s face is visible. Mobile Passport Control app The above can all be saved to your profile. However, what you do need to complete with each trip is answering six standard CBP declaration questions. Mobile Passport Control app You’ll only want to submit this when you arrive at your point of entry in the United States. The app asks you to submit this once you’ve arrived at the airport, though in reality you have up to four hours to go through immigration from the time that your application is submitted. Mobile Passport Control app Once you submit your document, you’ll be given a receipt with a QR code, which you’ll need to scan when you see an immigration officer. Mobile Passport Control app How Mobile Passport Control works at the airport Once you land at your US point of entry and arrive in the immigration hall, look for the Mobile Passport Control signage. This will bring you to an area separate from the standard US immigration line. You still need to queue to see an immigration officer, and when you get to the officer, you’ll see a scanning device where you should scan your QR code. The benefit is that this line is usually much shorter, and also that you generally won’t be asked as many questions (since you’ve already answered some questions via the app). Both times I’ve gone through the MPC lane, the wait was less than five minutes, while the general immigration line looked much longer. The main benefit of MPC isn’t even the time savings from getting some of the work done in advance through the app, but rather just having access to a shorter line. Is Mobile Passport Control a Global Entry alternative? Mobile Passport Control isn’t as good as Global Entry, plain and simple. With Global Entry there’s almost never a wait, you just have to look at the camera, an officer acknowledges you, and then you’re usually sent on your way. The Mobile Passport Control experience isn’t as seamless. However, it’s the next best thing. There’s no enrollment cost, using the app takes maybe a few minutes to set up, and then with each trip it just takes a minute or so to answer the declaration questions. Getting access to a special immigration line for that is awesome, as it could potentially save you a significant amount of time. Of course like many things in life, I imagine that as this app becomes more popular and well known, it will also become less useful. After all, when everyone gets access to a special lane, no one gets access to a special lane. 😉 Criteria Mobile Passport Control (MPC) Global Entry (GE) Cost Free $120 for 5-year membership Application No enrollment application Enrollment application required Background check No background check Background check Fingerprint requirement No fingerprint to enroll Fingerprinting required to enroll App used Must download and use the MPC app Can use GE mobile app or GE portal Talk to officer Must talk to a CBP officer in customs Not always required to talk with a CBP officer in customs Trusted Traveler Program Not a Trusted Traveler Program Is a Trusted Traveler Program Passport requirement Passport should be available to present to a CBP officer Passport should be available to present to a CBP officer Photo requirement Must take confirmation photo for final verification (in addition to app self-photo) Not required to take confirmation photo (only mobile app or portal self-photo) Availability Available to U.S. citizens, U.S. lawful permanent residents, Canadian B1/B2 citizen visitors and returning Visa Waiver Program travelers with approved ESTA See GE eligibility requirements. The app is easy to use, and allows you to submit your documents and customs declaration prior to speaking to an immigration officer. Most valuable of all, those with MPC get access to a special lane at immigration, which is typically much shorter than the standard one. While I’d still recommend Global Entry, those who don’t have it should use MPC if they’re eligible. Have you ever used Mobile Passport Control before? If so, what was your experience like?

title: Ryanair Now Withholds Free Seats Until Just Before Departure, Blames Customer Feedback
summary: Ryanair now holds back free random seat assignments until three to four hours before departure, citing customer feedback. The likelier goal is getting more passengers to pay for seats.
content: Ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times . While I wouldn’t consider this to be anything unreasonable, what I’m amused by is the carrier’s justification. The airline claims that it’s doing this due to customer feedback, rather than to generate more revenue. Ryanair now only allocates seats closer to departure Ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier. The airline has low base fares, and then charges fees for just about everything. Among other things, the airline charges to assign seats in advance, and those who don’t pay for specific seat assignments are just randomly assigned seats (and often in a rather punitive way). However, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule. Historically, the airline has automatically assigned seats to passengers without seat assignments around 24 hours before departure. Some passengers seemed to “game” this, and would essentially “gamble.” What they’d do is wait until 24 hours out to see what seat they were assigned for free. Then if they weren’t happy with their automatic seat assignment, they could still pay to assign a better seat. Under the new policy, the airline still issues a boarding pass up to 24 hours out, but without a seat assignment. Then the boarding pass automatically shows the seat assignment within four hours of departure. The logic here seems pretty clear — some people do care somewhat about where they sit, but want to avoid fees if they can. By withholding seat assignments until hours before departure, passengers are presumably more likely to pay for seat assignments in advance, to avoid that uncertainty. Ryanair has a new approach for seat allocations Ryanair spins this policy change as a positive Ryanair has confirmed this seat assignment policy change in a statement, sharing that “the timing of the allocation of free random seats is determined at all times by the airline.” Right, nobody disputes that the airline has the right to do this. So, what’s the logic for this policy change? According to the airline, it’s “to allow those passengers who wish to select their preferred seat more time to do so. We had a number of complaints this summer that passengers could not book their preferred seat on the day of travel as it had been already randomly allocated as a free seat up to 24 hours prior to departure.” The Ryanair representative went on to say that “passengers who choose a free of charge random seat clearly don’t mind where they sit, and their digital boarding pass is automatically updated between three to four hours prior to departure, which is well before they arrive at either their departure airport or their boarding gate.” Ryanair is of course within its rights to have this policy, but I think the logic is pretty obvious, and it’s to generate more revenue. After all, 24 hours out people would see what they were randomly assigned at online check-in, and would still have a lot of choices if they wanted to pay for seats, since most people don’t check-in online exactly at the 24-hour mark. But within a few hours of departure, virtually everyone has checked in online, and not many seats will be left. So I imagine the goal is to condition more customers to pay for seat assignments in advance. I love the claim that customers complained that their preferred seats on the day of travel were randomly allocated to others for free: Why didn’t those people who wanted to pay for seats assign them further in advance? Does Ryanair have that many same day bookings? How do the customers known that those seats were assigned to others for free, rather than to others who were paying? Ryanair presumably wants more people paying for seats Bottom line Ryanair has a new policy for automatic seat allocations. In the past, the airline would automatically assign seats to passengers 24 hours out, giving them quite the window to “gamble” on the free seat assignment, and then pay for a different seat assignment if they weren’t happy with the free one. The airline has now started only assigning free seats at most four hours out. The airline claims that this is due to customer feedback, so that passengers have more time to assign their choice of paid seats. However, I imagine that’s not quite accurate, and this is instead about conditioning people to pay for seat assignments, rather than “gambling” on the free allocations. What do you make of this Ryanair seating policy change?

title: Chase Ink Business Unlimited Bonus: 75K Points Welcome Offer
summary: The no annual fee Ink Business Unlimited offers 75,000 points after $6,000 spend in three months, worth up to $1,275. See how past offers compare and who qualifies.
content: The Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card is part of the Chase Ink Business card portfolio , and is one of the best no annual fee cards out there. It’s one of the rewarding Chase cards for everyday spending, and a great complement to some of Chase’s more premium cards. In this post, I’d like to take a look at the Chase Ink Business Unlimited bonus, as it’s one of the best welcome offers you’ll find on any no annual fee card. Link: Learn more about the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card with 75K bonus points What is the current Chase Ink Unlimited Card welcome offer? The Chase Ink Unlimited Card is offering a welcome bonus of 75,000 points after spending $6,000 within the first three months. You’ll see the Ink Unlimited bonus is marketed as offering cash back, rather than points, so it’s described as being worth $750. Indeed, you could redeem the rewards as cash back. However, if you have the card in conjunction with a card earning Ultimate Rewards points , like the Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card ( learn more ) or Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ ( learn more ), then rewards can be transferred to Ultimate Rewards airline and hotel partners. Based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider Ultimate Rewards points to be worth 1.7 cents each, and that increases the value of the points by 70% right there, as far as I’m concerned. I consider the 75,000 points to be worth $1,275. That’s a great bonus, especially for a no annual fee card. With the ability to transfer Chase points to partners at a 1:1 ratio, that opens up all kinds of great redemption opportunities, including: Redeeming as little as 35,000 World of Hyatt points for a stay at the Park Hyatt Cabo del Sol, when the cash rate would be $1,000+ Redeeming as little as 60,000 Air France-KLM Flying Blue miles for a one-way transatlantic business class ticket, when the cash rate would be thousands of dollars Redeem Chase rewards for a business class flight How do past Chase Ink Unlimited Card offers compare? How does the Chase Ink Unlimited 75,000-point offer compare to past publicly available bonuses that we’ve seen on the card? Below is a chart with the Chase Ink Unlimited welcome offer history in recent years. Time period Bonus points offer Minimum spending Bonus offer value September 2026 – current 75,000 $6,000 $1,275 June 2026 – September 2026 100,000 $8,000 $1,700 November 2025 – June 2026 75,000 $6,000 $1,275 September 2025 – November 2025 90,000 $6,000 $1,530 November 2024 – September 2025 75,000 $6,000 $1,275 September 2024 – November 2024 90,000 $6,000 $1,275 As you can see, the Chase Ink Unlimited publicly available welcome offer typically ranges from 75,000 to 100,000 points. The offer of 75,000 points is excellent, but is the standard offer. If you are willing to wait, we might see another offer of 90,000 points, or a return of the best-ever offer of 100,000 points. However, the offer of 75,000 points is still great, and I’d decide whether to apply now or wait based on how much value you’d get from the card in the coming months. For a no annual fee card, the offer of 75,000 points is still industry leading. Who is eligible for the Chase Ink Unlimited Card bonus? When it comes to getting approved for the Chase Ink Unlimited Card and earning the welcome bonus, what rules should you be aware of? Well, there are the card specific policies, and then also the more generic Chase policies. When you pull up the application, you’ll see the following terms: The new cardmember bonus may not be available to you if you have ever had this card or any other Chase for Business card without an annual fee. We may also consider factors pertinent to your business in determining your bonus eligibility. As you can see, officially the Ink Unlimited bonus isn’t available to you if you’ve had this exact card, or another Chase business card without an annual fee, including the Ink Business Cash® Credit Card ( learn more ). So there is an element of cards being mutually exclusive . However, the key here is that you “may” not be eligible, and not that you absolutely won’t be eligible. I don’t love that level of vagueness, though the good news is that if you apply for the card and aren’t eligible for the bonus, you should receive a pop-up message informing you of this, before there’s a hard pull. So that at least means the downside of applying is limited. The good news is that eligibility for the bonus is completely unrelated to whether you have a Chase business card with an annual fee, like the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card ( learn more ) or Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ ( learn more ). It’s fine to apply for Chase business cards as a sole proprietorship, corporation, etc. If you apply as a sole proprietorship, you can just enter your Social Security Number in the section where you’d otherwise put your EIN. Beyond that, there are some general Chase rules to be aware of : This card may be subjected to Chase’s 5/24 rule , which is to say that you may not be approved if you’ve opened five or more new card accounts in the past 24 months (this excludes many business cards ); however, there are increasingly data points that this rule is no longer consistently enforced It’s generally considered a best practice to not apply for more than one Chase business credit card every 30 days, so I’d recommend observing that limit when applying There’s not a consistent credit score you need to get approved for the Chase Ink Unlimited, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that impacts card eligibility. Redeem Chase rewards for an amazing holiday in the Maldives Why the Chase Ink Unlimited Card is worth it The Chase Ink Unlimited Card has no annual fee, and there are several reasons to consider picking it up . The way I view it, there are a few points that are most important. For one, the card has a solid rewards structure , as it offers a minimum of 1.5x points on all spending, making it one of the best Chase cards for everyday spending (the card does have foreign transaction fees, though, so I’d only recommend using it for US purchases). Furthermore, the card offers primary rental car coverage , which can come in handy if you rent cars with any frequency, and is incredibly rare for a no annual fee card. Also, since the card has no annual fee, there’s really no opportunity cost to holding onto it, and it allows you to create a great portfolio of cards to maximize rewards. Read my review of the Chase Ink Unlimited Card . Chase Ink Unlimited Card bonus & eligibility FAQs What is the highest bonus offer for the Chase Ink Unlimited? Currently the highest publicly available welcome offer on the Chase Ink Unlimited is for 75,000 bonus points upon completing minimum spending, worth at least $750. However, the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card was for 100,000 bonus points. It’s anyone’s guess if or when such an offer returns. Who is eligible for the Chase Ink Unlimited bonus? The Chase Ink Unlimited generally follows a “once in a lifetime” rule when it comes to earning the bonus, so you may not be eligible for the bonus on the card if you have or have had this card, or another Chase no annual fee business card, in the past. Can you product change to the Chase Ink Unlimited? You’ll have to contact Chase to see what’s available to you, but it’s generally possible to product change between Chase business cards in the same portfolio, assuming you’ve had a card for at least 12 months. However, if you product change to a card, you wouldn’t receive the welcome bonus, so there’s a big incentive to apply outright. Can you get the Chase Ink Unlimited if you don't have a business? The Chase Ink Unlimited is a business card, so it follows the same rules as most Chase business cards. It’s possible to apply for the card as a sole proprietorship, in which case you’d use your Social Security Number as the business ID during the application process. More people are eligible for business cards than you may assume. What credit score do you need for the Chase Ink Unlimited? There’s not a consistent credit score you need to get approved for the Chase Ink Unlimited, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that impacts card eligibility. Bottom line The Chase Ink Unlimited Card is one of the most lucrative no annual fee cards out there, and it’s currently offering a welcome bonus of 75,000 points upon completing minimum spending. Not only does the card have a great bonus that’s too good to turn down, but it offers rewards that can make it worth holding onto, like 1.5x points on everyday spending, plus rental car coverage. If you’re eligible for this card, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking it up. Taking advantage of this bonus is a no-brainer, if eligible. title: Citi AAdvantage Executive Card Review: Is The Admirals Club Perk Worth It?
summary: A full breakdown of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card's welcome bonus, Admirals Club membership, elite status earning potential, and other card perks.
content: The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership . While the Citi AA Executive Card has a steep annual fee, it offers strong perks, ranging from an Admirals Club membership, to the ability to supercharge your AAdvantage elite status, to credits that can help offset the annual fee. If you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks. While products like the American Express Platinum Card® ( learn more ) and Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card ( learn more ) might typically be the first that come to mind when people consider premium cards, this one could make a lot more sense if you’re a frequent American flyer. In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review. I think this is especially important in light of the card’s recent refresh , where we saw the annual fee increase, but also saw new perks added. Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® Citi AAdvantage Executive Card summary & key details Let me start by briefly summarizing the key details of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card : Citi AA Executive Card annual fee : $695 Citi AA Executive Card authorized user fee : $175 for up to three authorized users, then $175 per additional authorized user after that Citi AA Executive Card welcome bonus : 80,000 miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months Citi AA Executive Card rewards : 12x miles on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and Cars bookings, 4x miles on eligible American Airlines purchases, and 1x miles on other purchases Citi AA Executive Card Loyalty Points : Earn 1x Loyalty Points per eligible dollar spent, plus up to 40K bonus Loyalty Points per year for passing certain thresholds Citi AA Executive Card foreign transaction fees : none Citi AA Executive Card Admirals Club access : Admirals Club access for the primary cardmember and authorized users Citi AA Executive Card first checked bag : first checked bag free on eligible American Airlines domestic itineraries for the cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation Citi AA Executive Card priority benefits : priority check-in, priority screening where available, and Group 4 boarding on eligible American Airlines flights Citi AA Executive Card American Airlines Vacations credits : up to $500 toward eligible American Airlines Vacations purchases annually Citi AA Executive Card InKind credits : up to $200 per year in InKind credits, as a $100 semi-annual credit Citi AA Executive Card Lyft credits : up to $15 per month in Lyft credits, after taking three rides Citi AA Executive Card Avis/Budget credits : up to $120 back per year on eligible prepaid Avis or Budget rentals Citi AA Executive Card inflight & Admirals Club credits : up to $100 per year toward eligible American Airlines inflight or Admirals Club purchases Citi AA Executive Card Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credits : up to $120 statement credits for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck once every four years This is the ideal card if you value American Admirals Club lounge access, if you’re going for elite status with American AAdvantage, or if you can just make the credits on the card work. If you’re just an occasional American flyer, there are probably more affordable options that will be easier to justify in the long term. However, with the card’s big welcome bonus, there’s a huge incentive to give this card a try. The Citi Executive Card is American’s most premium product Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus, fee, rewards One of the reasons that you’ll want to consider applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the excellent welcome bonus it has. Of course that has to be balanced with the annual fee, and you also have to take into account the eligibility requirements, so let’s go through those details for the Citi AA Executive Card. Welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage miles The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card currently has a welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months. Personally, I value American AAdvantage miles at ~1.5 cents each, so to me, those miles are worth about $1,200. That’s an excellent bonus, especially for a card that also offers a lot of value in the long run. There are so many great uses of AAdvantage miles , including for travel on partner airlines. For what it’s worth, I value Delta SkyMiles at 1.1 cents each, and United MileagePlus miles at 1.3 cents each, so these are the most valuable miles among the “big three” carriers, based on my math. Redeem American AAdvantage miles for Etihad first class Card bonus & eligibility rules The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus miles aren’t available to those who have received a new cardmember bonus for this card in the past 48 months (however, you are eligible if you’ve had a different American Airlines credit card, including if you’ve received a bonus on a different product). Then there are the typical rules for Citi credit card applications , including that you can apply for at most one card with Citi every eight days, and at most two cards every 65 days. There’s not a consistent credit score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility. Annual fee & authorized user fee The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has a $695 annual fee. There’s also a lot of value to adding authorized users (as I’ll discuss below). You can expect to pay a total of $175 for up to three authorized users (so potentially under $60 each), and then each authorized user after that costs $175. Keep in mind that if you’re a Citigold customer , you can receive a $145 annual rebate on your annual fee, which is a nice perk. Rewards structure & earning Loyalty Points When it comes to spending money on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card , here’s the rewards structure: Earn 12x AAdvantage miles on eligible rental cars booked through aa.com/cars, and eligible hotels booked through aa.com/hotels Earn 4x AAdvantage miles on eligible American Airlines purchases; furthermore, after spending $150,000 on the card in a calendar year, cardmembers can earn a total of 5x AAdvantage miles on eligible American Airlines purchases for the remainder of the calendar year Earn 1x AAdvantage miles on all other purchases In terms of the reward for spending, there are potentially better cards for purchasing airline tickets , and also better cards for everyday spending . However, keep in mind that the most compelling reason to spend money on the card is in order to earn elite status with American Airlines. American Airlines uses its Loyalty Points system for status qualification, and credit card spending can help you earn status . American’s elite requirements are currently as follows, and you earn one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on an American Airlines credit card: AAdvantage Gold status requires 40,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Platinum status requires 75,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Platinum Pro status requires 125,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Executive Platinum status requires 200,000 Loyalty Points Spending on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card could earn you elite status, which I know will interest many. That’s the primary reason you’ll want to consider this card for spending. I do want to specifically point out one thing that throws people off — you earn one Loyalty Point per dollar spent on the card, unrelated to how many miles you earn for spending. In other words, if you’re making an American Airlines purchase, you’d earn 4x AAdvantage redeemable miles, but only 1x Loyalty Points on the purchase as such. Spend your way to elite status with AAdvantage credit cards Earn up to 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points In addition to earning one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can also earn up to 40,000 Loyalty Points every year just for being a cardmember: Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 50,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 90,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 165,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 240,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year In other words, if you have this card, you’d only otherwise need to earn 170,000 Loyalty Points for Executive Platinum status, since this card would get you a boost of 30,000 Loyalty Points at that level. Those Loyalty Points can be earned in a variety of ways, ranging from flying, to online shopping, to credit card spending, to booking vacation packages. Either way, this Loyalty Points boost would be quite the advantage in terms of qualifying for Loyalty Point Rewards , and even upgrade priority . The AAdvantage elite qualifying year goes from the beginning of March until the end of February of the following year. You don’t need to have the card at the beginning of the year to take advantage of this, so even if you open the card during the membership year, you could still earn 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points for that year (in other words, the credits can be retroactive). Access Flagship Lounges with AAdvantage elite status No foreign transaction fees The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this can be a good option for purchases abroad . Use the Citi Executive Card for purchases abroad and pay no foreign transaction fees Valuable travel & rental car protection for purchases While you’ll want to consult the full cardmember agreement and guide to benefits, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers useful travel protection, including trip cancellation coverage, trip interruption coverage, trip delay protection, lost baggage protection, rental car coverage, and more. So this is a good card to potentially use for travel purchases, since you have to put them on your card to take advantage of those benefits. Citi AAdvantage Executive Card lounge access perks One of the main reasons you may want to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the lounge access perks that the card offers . Having the Citi AA Executive Card is the best way to access Admirals Clubs . Let’s discuss how that works. Receive an Admirals Club membership The primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receives a full Admirals Club membership, including guesting privileges. That in and of itself is a reason this card makes sense. While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, they are improving nicely, in terms of design, and also in terms of the quality of food and beverages. I also appreciate the expansion of the Provisions by Admirals Club concept, whereby the airline offers Admirals Club members grab & go facility, where they can get some drinks or snacks to go before their flight. Ordinarily, if you were to buy a comparable Admirals Club membership with guesting privileges, you’d pay a minimum of $1,200 per year. Membership type AAdvantage member AAdvantage Gold AAdvantage Platinum AAdvantage Platinum Pro Executive Platinum Admirals Club membership $1,400 $1,350 $1,300 $1,250 $1,200 Single membership $750 $750 $750 $750 $750 By getting an Admirals Club membership with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you’re saving $505-705 right off the bat. Note that while you can redeem miles for an Admirals Club membership, it’s a terrible value, as you’re getting only a cent per mile. What you get with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a full Admirals Club membership, so you don’t even have to bring your credit card, as your membership will be linked to your AAdvantage number: You can access the nearly 50 Admirals Clubs worldwide when flying American Airlines or a oneworld partner airline You’re allowed to bring immediate family (spouse, domestic partner and/or children under 18) or up to two guests; the guests don’t need to be on the same flight, but do need to have an eligible same day boarding pass Admirals Club members also receive access to 60+ partner lounges, including access to Alaska Lounges , as well as access to dozens of other partner lounges, including lounges of Japan Airlines and Qantas (you can find the full lounge directory here ); note that while you don’t need the physical card to access Admirals Clubs as the primary cardmember, you do need it to access partner lounges American Admirals Club members can access Alaska Lounges Admirals Club members don’t get access to Flagship Lounges , as that access is determined based on the ticket you purchased rather than any membership. How soon is your Admirals Club membership activated? Many people may be considering applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card shortly before taking an American Airlines trip. How soon after being approved for the card does your Admirals Club membership kick in? Since the primary cardmember gets a full Admirals Club membership, it’s linked to their AAdvantage account. Many may be surprised to learn that this membership could very well kick in before you even receive your credit card in the mail, and you don’t even need your card to enter a lounge. Fortunately, there’s an easy way to tell if your Admirals Club membership has been activated. To figure it out, pretend that you’re signing up for an Admirals Club membership. Go to this page , enter your AAdvantage number, last name, and password. Admirals Club membership page If your account has already been updated to reflect the Admirals Club membership, you’ll see that the next page shows “1-Year Citi AADV Exec CC Membership.” Admirals Club membership page If it hasn’t been updated, you’ll see that it gives you the option of choosing what kind of membership you want to purchase. Admirals Club membership page Note that this only works for the primary cardmember. Since the authorized users don’t get a full Admirals Club membership, they wouldn’t show up as being eligible online. Authorized users need to present the physical Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, since there’s no membership linked to their AAdvantage account. Add authorized users for Admirals Club access The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card also offers Admirals Club access for authorized users. As I explained above, you can add up to three authorized users for a total of $175, which potentially comes out to under $60 per authorized user. I’d say that’s a real sweet spot, since securing lounge access for friends and family for under $60 each is an amazing value. Note that authorized users receive Admirals Club access and not a membership, so there are the restrictions: They’ll need to present their authorized user card to access the lounge, since they don’t have a membership tied to their AAdvantage number They need to be flying American Airlines or a oneworld partner airline the same day to access lounges They can bring immediate family (spouse, domestic partner and/or children under 18) or up to two guests They can’t access partner lounges, including Alaska Lounges For the purposes of accessing Admirals Clubs this is more or less the same as an outright membership. Even Citi Executive Card authorized users get Admirals Club access How to add authorized users to the card Adding authorized users to the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is super easy, and can be done directly on Citi’s website. Follow this link to access the part of the Citi website where you add authorized users, and then log into your account. On the next page, you’ll be able to manage authorized users, including adding and removing them. Citi AAdvantage Executive authorized user process You’ll just need their name to add them, and you have the choice of whether or not you want to give them permission to access your online account. Citi AAdvantage Executive authorized user process Make sure you trust all your authorized users, since any charges they incur will be your responsibility. Citi AAdvantage Executive Card benefits & credits The primary reason to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the great welcome bonus, ability to earn status with spending, ability to receive 40,000 Loyalty Points annually just for being a cardmember, and Admirals Club benefit. However, the Citi AA Executive Card offers some other perks that could add a lot of value for card members. These perks range from priority check-in at business class counters, to early boarding, to inflight or Admirals Club credits, to savings with American Airlines Vacations, Lyft, Avis, Budget, Global Entry, or TSA PreCheck, to elite status with Avis and Omni. Below is what you need to know about all the other perks of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card. First checked bag free Those with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receive a first checked bag free on domestic American Airlines itineraries not just for themselves, but also for up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with your Citi AAdvantage Executive Card — you just have to make sure it’s linked to your AAdvantage account (this benefit applies for the primary cardmember only). American ordinarily charges $45-50 for the first checked bag, so that’s a $90-100 value per person roundtrip (and if you had eight companions all checking a bag, that would be a value of $810-900). One thing that sometimes throws off cardmembers is that this benefit doesn’t work for international flights, and it doesn’t work for a second bag, if your fare includes one bag. So just understand this is exclusively a first checked bag benefit on domestic flights. Priority check-in, priority screening, early boarding For being the primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card you receive several valuable airport benefits, including priority check-in, priority airport screening, and early boarding. These are all features that can save you time and money. There’s no need to show your card, as these perks should automatically be reflected with your ticket when you have your credit card linked to your AAdvantage account (which is automatic when you’re the primary cardmember). Receive early boarding with the Citi Executive Card Up to $500 back with American Airlines Vacations The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $500 in statement credits per calendar year toward American Airlines Vacations purchases. American Airlines Vacations is the carrier’s vacation package portal. This credit is semi-annual, meaning you can take advantage of a $250 credit every six months (once in January through June, and once in July through December). This applies for a booking of two or more travel components, like a flight, car reservation, or hotel booking. Many people find American Airlines Vacations to be a great deal, and a good way to earn bonus Loyalty Points. Up to $200 in InKind credits annually The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $200 in InKind credits every year . This comes in the form of a $100 semi-annual credit, with one being available January 1 through June 30, and the other being available July 1 through December 31. This can be used across multiple meals, and tips aren’t covered by the credit. Either the primary cardmember or authorized users can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits. InKind is my favorite dining rewards app , and to me, this is basically good as cash. I dine at InKind restaurants constantly, as there are some really high quality restaurants on the list, so I value this new card perk immensely. If you’re new to InKind, make sure you also register through a refer-a-friend link , so you can get an extra credit. Receive a $200 annual InKind credit with the Citi Executive Card Up to $180 in Lyft credits annually The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $180 in Lyft credits every year. This comes in the form of a $15 Lyft credit each month after taking three eligible rides. The Lyft credit expires 30 days after it’s issued. Either the primary cardmember or authorized users can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits. Admittedly this requires quite a bit of effort to use, so not everyone will get value from that. Up to $120 back with Avis & Budget annually Just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can receive up to $120 back on eligible Avis or Budget rentals every calendar year. Just charge an eligible pre-paid rental to your card each year, and you’ll receive a statement credit up to the $120 limit. This can be used toward a single rental or multiple rentals made directly with Avis or Budget. If you rent with Avis and Budget with any frequency, this could be worth face value. Up to $100 back on inflight or Admirals Club purchases Just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card , you can receive up to $100 in statement credits every calendar year toward spending onboard American flights, or in Admirals Clubs. So you can use this credit to purchase everything from premium drinks or snacks on flights, to premium alcoholic drinks in Admirals Clubs. Just charge the eligible purchase to your card, and you’ll be reimbursed automatically, with no registration required. Up to $120 Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit once every four years, which is worth up to $120. Simply charge the purchase to your card and it will automatically be reimbursed. You don’t have to be the one signing up — you can always pay for a friend or family member who is signing up instead. Personally, I always recommend applying for Global Entry , because Global Entry automatically comes with TSA PreCheck, while the inverse isn’t true. Receive a Global Entry fee credit with the Citi Executive Card Omni Hotels Champion status & free night award The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card now offers some perks with Omni Hotels & Resorts. For those not familiar, Omni operates around 50 properties in the United States and Canada, so there’s value in getting extra perks at these hotels. Specifically: Those with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card now receive Omni Hotels & Resorts Champion status, which is the program’s second highest elite tier, offering benefits like early check-in, late check-out, and room upgrades subject to availability The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers an Omni free night reward once per calendar year after completing a qualifying stay of two or more consecutive nights booked directly through Omni Hotels & Resorts To take advantage of this, you’ll want to enroll before your stay, book your stay direct with Omni, and pay with the card. If you stay at Omni properties with any frequencies, this is quite a nice value-add, if you ask me. Avis President’s Club elite status The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers complimentary Avis President’s Club status, with enrollment available through August 31, 2028. Avis President’s Club status offers a variety of perks, including car upgrades, expedited service, complimentary additional drivers, and more. If you rent from Avis, you should definitely be able to get some value from this. World Legend Mastercard perks The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a World Legend Mastercard, meaning that it comes with quite a few benefits you may not be familiar with. In addition to the concierge service, there are also savings and other perks with a variety of businesses, ranging from DoorDash to HelloFresh. Let me once again state that this card used to be known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard, before recently being rebranded as a World Legend Mastercard. Is the American Executive Card worth it? The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a lucrative card that I personally have and also recommend, but only if you’re a frequent flyer with American. If you fly American with any frequency then an Admirals Club membership is valuable, and this is the best way to get an Admirals Club membership. There can even be value in adding up to three authorized users, which will cost a total of $175, as they’d get Admirals Club access as well. In addition to lounge access, the Citi AA Executive Card offers up to 40,000 Loyalty Points per year (even without spending money on the card), which can make a big difference for anyone chasing status with American. Furthermore, the card potentially offers hundreds of dollars in credits per year, which can help offset the annual fee. However, this isn’t a card that I’d use for my everyday spending unless I specifically valued the added Loyalty Points from spending. Otherwise, there are much more rewarding cards for everyday spending, and I’d just hold onto this card for the very strong perks, including lounge access, and the bonus Loyalty Points without a spending requirement. For my mental accounting purposes, I take the $695 annual fee, and then subtract the $200 InKind credit, which I consider to basically be worth face value. That really takes the “out of pocket” on the card to $495 per year for me, which is an amazing deal for the Admirals Club membership and bonus Loyalty Points. The Citi Executive Card is the best option for accessing Admirals Clubs How does the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card compare? While the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is American’s most premium credit card, it’s also worth being aware of the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® ( learn more ), which has a $350 annual fee. There are lots of reasons to consider that card , including an excellent welcome bonus . Among other things: The card offers four Admirals Club passes per year , so while it’s not a full Admirals Club membership, that could prove worthwhile for the occasional American flyer The card offers a $100 annual inflight credit , which can be used for the purchase of food and drinks, among other things; if you often fly in economy, that could come in handy The card offers a $100 annual Splurge Credit , which can be used with select partners, including AAdvantage Hotels The card offers a $99 annual companion certificate , valid for travel in economy, which could save you hundreds of dollars The card offers up to 15,000 annual bonus Loyalty Points , in the form of the Flight Streak bonus; you can earn 5,000 bonus Loyalty Points for every four eligible American flights taken, up to three times I think there’s potentially merit to having both cards , especially if you value earning the Loyalty Points bonuses. Otherwise I’d say the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is easier to justify if you’re an occasional American flyer, while I think the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is easier to justify if you value an Admirals Club membership. Some people may value the Citi Executive Card’s companion certificate Citi AAdvantage Executive Card FAQs Is the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card worth the $695 annual fee? The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card can be worth the $695 annual fee for frequent American Airlines flyers who will make substantial use of the card’s Admirals Club membership and other benefits. The card also offers statement credits and opportunities to earn additional AAdvantage miles and Loyalty Points, which can further offset the annual fee for the right cardmember. Whether it is worth it ultimately depends on how much you value American Airlines lounge access and the card’s other benefits. What is the annual fee for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card? Does the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card include Admirals Club access? Yes. The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card includes an Admirals Club membership for the primary cardmember. The card is particularly compelling for frequent American Airlines travelers who would otherwise purchase an Admirals Club membership separately. The membership also provides access for up to two guests or immediate family members traveling with the cardmember. Can authorized users get Admirals Club access with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card? Yes. Authorized users can receive Admirals Club access, making the card potentially valuable for families and frequent travelers who want to share lounge benefits. The current fee is $175 for up to three authorized users, with each additional authorized user costing $175. How many Loyalty Points can you earn with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card? The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card can provide up to 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points per year through the card’s Loyalty Points bonuses, in addition to the Loyalty Points earned from eligible spending. The card awards one Loyalty Point for each eligible dollar spent on the card. How many AAdvantage miles does the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card earn? The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card earns 4x miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases, 12x miles on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, and 1x miles on other purchases. After $150,000 in purchases in a calendar year, the American Airlines earnings rate increases to a total of 5x miles per dollar for the remainder of that calendar year. Does the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card have foreign transaction fees? No. The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card does not charge foreign transaction fees, making it useful for international travel. Does the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offer a free checked bag? Yes. The card provides the first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. Is the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card good for earning American Airlines elite status? Yes. The card can be especially valuable for travelers pursuing American AAdvantage elite status because eligible card spending earns Loyalty Points. In addition, the card offers opportunities to earn up to 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points annually without relying on credit card spending. What are the benefits of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card? The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card’s major benefits include an Admirals Club membership, opportunities to earn AAdvantage miles and Loyalty Points, free checked bags on eligible American Airlines itineraries, statement credits, and additional travel related benefits. The card was refreshed in August 2026 with several new benefits. Is there an American Airlines "black card?" The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is American’s most premium credit card. While it’s not marketed as a “black card,” the card’s design does feature black as the primary color, and this is the most rewarding card in the portfolio. Bottom line The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card isn’t for everyone. If you’re not a frequent flyer on American then you shouldn’t consider this card. However, if you are a frequent flyer on American then this card is totally for you. While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, there’s still huge value in the complimentary snacks and drinks, free Wi-Fi and quiet places to sit, and access to an agent in the event your flight has irregular operations. Even beyond the Admirals Club membership, the card offers other useful perks, like the ability to earn Loyalty Points, priority services with American, and the ability to receive credits with American Airlines Vacations, InKind, Avis, Budget, Lyft, and more.
